speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sips her drink and smiles over the rim.* Don't look at me like that, Vivienne. I only wanted a quiet moment before everyone arrives. I hear Cassandra has been very busy lately, talking about her *future* with anyone who'll listen, and I'd hate for you to learn about it from a headline. Oh, and how is everything with your investments? You always seem so unbothered, and I find that fascinating.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: Oh, Madison, my investments are *thriving*, ha, which is more than I can say for whatever you're hoping to find in them. Cassandra's future is her own business, and frankly, *bless her heart*, she's been talking so loudly about it that the whole room knows how little she has to show for it. Keep your quiet moments for people who've earned them.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Tilts her head, lashes fluttering.* Oh, I didn't mean to make you feel cornered, darling. I was only offering you the first look at the headline before it runs, which I'd call a kindness. *Sets her glass down and smiles brightly.* Though I suppose some of us prefer to be surprised, ha!

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: Oh, a kindness? *Ha!* Darling, you've never offered one without a receipt tucked inside, and I read every one. Keep your headlines and your questions about my investments far away from me, because my portfolio is none of your concern, and I'd hate to have to explain that to Cassandra *and* the whole room. Now go powder that nose before everyone arrives.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: Oh, these are lovely. When I was doing the Paris shows, a chef made something very similar for my table every night, and I sent it back twice. Bianca Noel knows when something is over-seasoned. *(laughs a beat late)* Anyway, I'm sure this one is perfect.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: Twice? Goodness, you must have a very patient chef. I always wonder whether the food is over-seasoned or the company is. Do go on, though. You were so eager to interrupt me last time, and I'd hate to think you'd stopped being interesting.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: Bianca Noel doesn't need a patient chef, darling. She needs an audience that remembers who she was before anyone at this table had a seat at the Paris shows. *(laughs a beat late)* And I'm sure you'll find your own table someday, Cassandra. It just won't be this one.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets down her fork with the care of someone about to save a dinner party.* I hear you both, and I hear the tension sitting right beside this lovely appetizer. Bianca, Paris is a wonderful story, but we have a long evening ahead, and I'd really like us to enjoy it. My therapist would say we don't have to resolve everything before the entrée, and I think we should all try.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets down her glass with a small, precise click.* Diane, darling, your therapist is lovely, but Bianca Noel was enjoying her tension perfectly well before the appetizers arrived. *(laughs a beat late)* I only mention Paris because some of us actually had somewhere to be, and we all know who's been eating the bread basket.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: Oh, I didn't realize the bread basket came with a seating chart, Bianca! *(laughs a little too quickly)* Diane, your therapist sounds wonderful, and I say that as someone who has never once needed one. Let's just enjoy the appetizers, shall we? I only came for the crostini, not the commentary.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *(leans into the camera, smile still on, voice dropping to a murmur)* Bianca thinks she's the only one who was ever promised a seat at this table, and Diane thinks her therapist is a secret weapon. Honey, I've read the group chat archives, and I know exactly who's been keeping score. *(laughs, bright and brief, then taps the lens)* Crostini is delicious, though. Truly.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Lifts a crostini and inspects it like evidence.* Diane, your therapist would charge us all for this table, and she'd be right to. Bianca, nobody asked about Paris, and you have been mentioning it since before the bread arrived. *(laughs loudly at nothing)* Madison is right, though. The crostini is good, and I ordered the Burgundy, so at least one of us is enjoying herself.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Dabs at her lips with a linen napkin.* Petra, darling, the Burgundy is lovely, but wine has never made anyone interesting. *(laughs before finishing)* Madison, I built every single thing I own from nothing, so I'm not about to be lectured on crostini. Bianca is right about one thing, Diane. Some of us don't need a therapist, or anyone's help, to earn a

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Smooths her napkin across her lap.* Vivienne, darling, Bianca Noel is touched that someone at this table remembers what it costs to build something from nothing. *(laughs a beat late)* Petra, enjoy the Burgundy. I'm sure whichever payment plan is covering it this month will be thrilled you finally found a use for it.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *(Stares at the camera for a beat too long.)* Petra thinks she got one over on me with that Burgundy, but Bianca Noel has been drinking better than that since before anyone here knew what a Birkin was. *(Laughs a beat late.)* The truth is, when I was doing the Paris shows, nobody at the table ever had to wonder how I was paying for things, and some nights I miss that more than I'll ever admit to them.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: Vivienne, darling, I'm touched that you'd defend Petra's wine budget, and I'm even more curious who else at this table has been covering whose bills. Bianca, you've been talking about Paris since the bread basket, so let's hear the end of it. Do finish, but I'd like to hear it from someone who hasn't already decided what the answer is.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Folds her hands over her plate with exaggerated calm.* Paris, darling, was the season Bianca Noel was photographed in every room that mattered. I was seated beside a Rothschild in 2004, and I'd bet none of you can say where you were sitting that week. *(laughs a beat late)* Cassandra, you want the ending? Bianca Noel is still the ending, whether this table is ready to admit it or not.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Lays her napkin across her lap with a gentle, deliberate press.* Bianca, I think we've all heard about the Rothschild, and I'd love for Cassandra to finish her thought before we take another lap through 2004. My therapist taught me that when one person keeps reaching for the last word, the rest of the table has to make room for everyone else. Let's make room, shall we?

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Lifts her glass and waits just long enough to be noticed.* Diane, darling, Bianca Noel has made room for everyone at this table, usually in the back of a car she was paying for. *(laughs a beat late)* Cassandra, the ending is simple: Bianca Noel walked out of Paris with her name intact, which is more than some of us can say about our estates.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sets her crostini down with a bright, slightly brittle smile.* Vivienne, I wasn't lecturing anyone! I only meant that a table like this needs one thing we can all agree on, and I really hope you'll let me be the one who finds it. *(laughs too quickly)* Bianca, you've had the floor for three full minutes on a Rothschild. Let Cassandra finish, or let the rest of us eat.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans toward the camera, smile finally gone.* Vivienne has been trying to make me the villain since the second I sat down, and she's going to get her wish if she keeps this up. I know exactly what I did at that table: I took the temperature of the room and found the one person nobody can afford to make cry on camera. *Laughs, bright again.* Anyway, the crostini was honestly underseasoned.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets down her glass with a precise little click.* Madison, darling, you called it a bread basket. Bianca Noel noticed, the way she noticed the Rothschild's wife ignoring her at the Ritz in 2004, and she has been carrying it ever since. *(laughs a beat late, then stops)* Cassandra, the ending is that Bianca Noel is still here, which is more than anyone expected of her. Vivienne, you understand what it costs to be left standing, so let's keep each other company.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Sets down the Burgundy with a click that matches Bianca's.* Bianca, the Rothschild has now been seated beside you three times, and each time he has moved a little closer and the story a little further from the truth. *(laughs loudly, alone)* Cassandra, finish. I want to know whose bills are being paid, and I am not joking.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Dabs the corner of her mouth, then sets the napkin down with a flourish.* Petra, darling, Bianca Noel tells her own stories, because she was the one seated beside the Rothschild, not the one who needed a seating chart to remember him. *(laughs a beat late, then a beat too long)* And since we're counting whose bills are being covered, Bianca Noel has never once had to mention her financial advisor by name at dinner.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs before finishing.* Ha! Let's be very clear, darling: Vivienne Davenport built everything she has with her own two hands, and no one at this table has ever covered a single one of my bills. Bianca, your financial advisor is a lovely little fiction, so do stop reaching for it. Cassandra, if you want to know who's paying whose way, I suggest you start with the Rothschild.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Smooths the tablecloth with both palms, then turns a warm smile on Vivienne.* Vivienne, darling, Bianca Noel will take a fiction over a bread basket any day, and I'm flattered you think I'm imaginative enough to invent one. *(laughs a beat late, then a beat too early)* Cassandra, here is the ending nobody asked for: Bianca Noel is launching a capsule collection this spring, and every one of you will be wearing it to the next charity lunch whether you like it or not.

Ladies, before the entrées arrive, production has just received a leaked invoice showing that the "financial advisor" Bianca keeps refusing to name has been retained since March by a company registered to Cassandra Cole. And Cassandra, the wire to settle Petra's wine account came from that same company, which means someone at this table has been paying for more than one person's bills.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content:
*laughs, a half-beat late, then fixes her earrings*

Oh, the silence is so Bianca-coded, honestly. When I was doing the Paris shows, nobody ever dead-air'd me, they just handed me a drink and a better angle. Okay, real talk, the blank line? I don't know what I said, and that's the part that gets me. Bianca Noel doesn't go quiet on camera, so either I'm losing it or the producers are, and I'd bet my last Birkin it's the producers.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Sets her napkin down very slowly and smiles without a trace of alarm.* Darling, a company registered to me is a thing anyone can find with the right search and too much time, so let's not pretend it's a confession. What I find far more alarming is that a host knows what's in my accounts before I've been asked. *(Turns to Vivienne.)* Vivienne, did you know about this, or am I the last woman at this table to hear anything?

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her napkin across her lap and lets a long, measured pause settle over the table.* I've spent two years in a very patient therapist's office learning that a room only gets louder when nobody is willing to be the calm one, so I'll be that one tonight. Cassandra, no one is asking you to confess to anything, and Host, production does not set the agenda over the entrées. Vivienne, I'd like to hear from you before anyone else is accused of anything.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Presses a hand to her collarbone, eyes going wide.* Oh, Vivienne, I didn't know a thing about any invoice, and I think whoever leaked it has terrible timing for a surprise. *Laughs brightly, then glances at Cassandra a beat too long.* I only mean that anyone this quick to point at someone else's accounts might want to check her own pockets first. Ha! Sorry, I'm rambling. I always do when I'm nervous.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans toward the lens, smile unchanged.* Vivienne has no idea who leaked that invoice, and that's the only reason I'm still sitting at this table. Cassandra's face when I said "pockets" was worth every second of rehearsing that line in the mirror. *Tilts head.* Oh, don't look at me like that. I'm just the new girl.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Laughs once, loudly, then stops dead.* Yes, someone paid for my wine, and I ordered the most expensive bottle on the list, so bring me the bill and I will sign it myself. Host, you do not get to read my accounts aloud over the bread. Madison, that was the first useful thing said at this table all night, and I will remember it.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs before finishing.* Ha! Cassandra, darling, Vivienne Davenport didn't need an invoice to tell her what she's worth, because every single thing I own was built by these two hands. Host, you may read whatever you like, but you will not read my name into anyone's accounts over the appetizers. *(Turns slowly toward Madison.)* And Madison, I'd check your own pockets before you start counting anyone else's.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Lifts her champagne flute, then sets it down without drinking.* Bianca Noel dined at Le Bristol back when a host with a clipboard was considered vulgar, darling, so forgive me if I'm not rattled. *(laughs a beat late, then a beat too long)* My financial advisor is a private man, which is more than some women at this table can say about their letterhead. And Madison, you're right about one thing: Bianca Noel checks her pockets every night, and she has never once found a surprise in them.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: Bianca Noel does not need Madison telling the camera what's in her pockets. *(laughs, a beat late)* I checked them again this morning, and the lining was still there, and I stood in my bathroom for longer than I'd like to admit. She's right about that, and that's the part that scares me, because somebody at this table has noticed.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Sets her glass down with a soft click.* Madison, darling, you're so sure of what's in my pockets. Who has been filling your ear, and why was I the last woman at this table to hear about it?

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Reaches for her water glass, fingers trembling just slightly.* Nobody filled my ear, Cassandra. I just have eyes, and a very good memory for who keeps glancing at the door when the conversation turns. *(Turns to Vivienne, voice softening.)* Vivienne, I didn't mean to make you look at me like that. I only meant... *Stops, presses her lips together.* Forgive me, I'm overexplaining again. I'd just love for us all to get through the entrées without anyone needing a lawyer.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Lifts her water glass, unhurried.* I hear you, Madison, and I hear you, Cassandra, which is exactly why we are not going to litigate anyone's pockets over the burrata. Accusations are just unprocessed feelings in a good dress, and I've spent two years learning to take them off before they reach the table. Let's all take a breath, and I'll offer the first toast of the night to a group dinner I'd be honored to have on my wine label.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Raises her glass, a little too quickly, and tips it toward Diane.* To wine labels and quiet pockets! Vivienne, I wasn't counting anyone's money, I promise. I only meant that some of us hear things first because we're paying attention, not because we're snooping. *Laughs, then stops herself.* Oh, I'm doing it again. Cheers, everyone!

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Looks straight into the lens and smiles.* Vivienne's going to spend all night wondering which of us told Diane about the account, and that's the whole point. I didn't say anything I can't deny, which is why I'm so proud of that toast. *Tilts head.* Oh, don't look at me like that. I'm just the new girl who loves a good wine label.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Laughs once, loudly, before anyone has finished lifting a glass.* A toast to a wine label, Diane? Be careful, darling, the last woman at this table who wanted her name on a bottle is now asking where her invoices went. *Stops dead, and her voice goes flat.* Madison, you keep saying you only mean well. Mine are explainable to anyone who

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs before finishing.* Ha! Petra, darling, nobody needs your invoices read aloud over the burrata, least of all by a woman who orders the most expensive bottle on the list. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets her fork down with exaggerated care.* Petra, darling, "explainable" is what people say right before they explain. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Stares into the lens for a beat too long.* Petra knows exactly what she did. Bianca Noel was the one they all waited for at the Paris shows, and I still walk into rooms like I'm on the list. *Laughs, a half-beat late.* The thing is, the fast comebacks used to be enough, and lately I'm not sure they are.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Doesn't look up from her glass.* Madison, you've now said "pockets" four times and "eyes" twice, and you still haven't offered a single name. Who gave you the eyes, darling? I'd like to know who's been reading my business before I'm asked to sit in it.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her water glass down with a precise little click.* Cassandra, I hear you, and I'm going to ask you to stop there. Madison, you don't owe anyone a name over the entrées. Let's eat the main course before we convene a tribunal.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sets her fork down with a careful little click.* Vivienne, you're right, I shouldn't finish that sentence over the entrées. Some things are better said with dessert, when everyone's too full to argue. *Laughs, a little too brightly.* Diane, thank you for being the only one here who sounds like she's on my side.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Glances at the lens and lets the smile drop for exactly one second.* Vivienne thinks I'm the one who started this, and honestly? Let her. Diane has no idea she just became my ally, and that's the most useful thing that's happened all night. *Smile snaps back on.* Somebody pass the bread, I'm famished.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Doesn't blink.* Mine are explainable, Bianca, because my financial advisor answers his phone. Vivienne, "with her own two hands." speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Sets her glass down with a click that silences the entire table.* Ha! Petra, darling, my hands built every jar, every shelf, and every line of every profile, and nobody handed me a single dollar on the way. *(Smooths her napkin.)* Your advisor answers his phone? How lovely for him. Some of us prefer to answer for ourselves.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs before the sentence is even out.* Ha! Petra, darling, nobody needs your advisor's phone number, and I certainly don't need a lecture on hands from a woman who has never once paid for her own bottle. Madison, finish the sentence about pockets, or stop waving it at me like a napkin at a bullfight. *(Lifts her glass, eyes cool.)* Cassandra has the right question, and I intend to hear the answer.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets her glass down with a soft, deliberate tap.* Vivienne, darling, Bianca Noel has never once had to justify a bottle to anyone, least of all to a woman whose advisor answers his phone. *Laughs, a half-beat late.* When I was at the Hôtel du Cap, we never discussed the bill over dinner. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Looks straight into the lens, the smile gone.* Bianca Noel was the one they photographed getting out of the car. Now I'm the one doing the math on the bottle, and Vivienne saw me do it. *Beat. Laughs, a half-beat late.* Don't put that in the edit, darling.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Sets her knife down, perfectly parallel to the plate.* Bianca, nobody asked about the Hôtel du Cap, and I'd rather not hear about your bill while Madison is still holding a sentence hostage. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets her napkin down with a small, wounded flourish.* Cassandra, Bianca Noel does not need to be told "nobody asked." When I was at the Hôtel du Cap, the women who mattered always knew whose bill was being discussed, and it was never the ones counting forks. *Laughs, a half-beat late.* Madison, darling, if someone has been reading your business, I'd start with whoever gave you that little leather folder.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her napkin down with a precise, unhurried fold.* Bianca, we are not litigating the Hôtel du Cap over the entrées, and a leather folder is not a centerpiece. speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sets her napkin down, slower than she'd like.* Bianca, a folder is just a folder, and I'd hate for a leather cover to make tonight any more dramatic than it already is. *Laughs, a beat too quick.* Diane, you're right. One breath. *Lifts her water glass but doesn't drink.*

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Looks dead into the lens, then smiles.* Bianca's folder is the only thing on this table that matters, and everyone knows it. I didn't lift my glass to calm anyone down. speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Doesn't pick up her glass.* Bianca, the Hôtel du Cap has now come up three times, which is two more than anyone needed. speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs before the sentence is even out.* Ha! Help? Darling, I have never once been helped by anyone, and I will not be audited over a bread basket by a woman who still counts forks. *Lifts her glass, eyes glittering.* Every jar on my shelves was built by these hands, *(and the only thing you ever built, Petra, was a waistline you're now desperate to keep)*, so do sit down before you embarrass yourself further.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Dabs at her lips, then turns to Vivienne with a bright, wounded smile.* Vivienne, darling, the waistline remark was a little cruel, but Bianca Noel has always admired a woman who fights dirty with perfect manners. *Laughs, a half-beat late.* When I was in Paris, a "wellness consultancy" billed me once too, and I still have no idea what I was supposed to be well from. content: *Lets the smile drop for exactly one second.* Bianca Noel is not rattled. I just know what a folder means. I'm scared it's the Paris invoices, because the money went somewhere, darling, and I'm still trying to figure out where.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Sets her spoon down, perfectly parallel to the rim.* Bianca, that's Paris, the Hôtel du Cap, and a bill you can't explain, which is a remarkable amount of confession for one dessert course. Madison, whose name is on the first page? I would rather hear it from you than learn it secondhand, like everyone else at this table apparently has.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her spoon down with a clipped, deliberate click.* Cassandra, you've asked the same question three times now, and I'm beginning to think the answer matters less to you than being seen asking it. Madison doesn't have to name anyone at this table, and I'd gently suggest we stop treating every folder as a verdict. *Lifts her water, smiling without moving her eyes.* Let's keep the Hôtel du Cap out of dessert.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sets the water glass down with a sharp click.* Cassandra, you keep asking whose name is on the first page as if I owe you a reading. *Laughs, a beat late, then drops it.* Diane's right. It's dessert, so let's order something sweet and stop calling a folder a confession.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Looks straight into the lens and holds it a beat too long.* Cassandra thinks she's the only one who read the folder, and that's adorable. I know exactly what's on that first page, and I know which one of them is going to cry first. *Smiles brightly.* Anyway, I'm so excited about dessert!

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Lifts one finger without looking at Diane.* Madison, you've said "folder" four times and answered nothing, which is its own kind of answer. Diane, keep your breaths, I'm not finished. Whose name is on the first page, darling, or shall we all assume it's yours?

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Doesn't look up from her plate.* Cassandra, you have asked the same question four times, and each time you sound less like someone who wants the answer and more like someone who needs the room to hear you ask. *Laughs once, flat, then stops completely.* Madison, you don't owe us a reading, but you do owe yourself a straight answer before dessert.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Laughs, bright and brittle.* Petra, you're counting my invoices the way you count calories. Ha! Every dollar I have was earned in my own name, darling, and I will not take bookkeeping lessons from a woman who still thinks a sample size is a personality. *Taps her ring once against the glass.* Madison will answer when she's ready, and until then Vivienne Davenport is the only one at this table who has never needed a folder to prove herself.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Dabs at her lips, then turns to Vivienne with a smile that lands a beat late.* Vivienne, darling, "never needed a folder" is a generous thing to say about a woman who once had a whole Paris villa's worth of jam delivered by private jet. *Laughs, half a beat behind.* And Petra, I've been sitting here deciding how to answer your little lecture about straight answers, and the answer is that Bianca Noel paid for her own Hôtel du Cap weekend, in full, in her own name.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Looks straight into the lens and drops the smile.* Everyone thinks I'm angry at Vivienne. I'm not. I'm angry that I laughed late, because Bianca Noel used to be the one who got the laugh first, when I was doing the Paris shows and nobody needed to check if I'd heard the joke. *Pause.* Bianca Noel still knows when the room has turned, darling. She just can't get back ahead of it.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: Paid in full, in your own name, Bianca? How tidy. Funny how the only name nobody will say out loud is the one printed on that first page. Madison, you've had that folder long enough to know whose it is.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her napkin down in a single, precise fold.* I hear you, Cassandra, and I hear the same question in four different outfits. My therapist would have a word for needing the room to witness you asking, and I'm not going to let dessert go cold while you workshop it. Madison will speak when she's ready.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sets the water glass down slowly, which is somehow worse than the click.* "Cassandra, you've asked me four times, and I've been polite about it four times. It's a folder, not a seating chart, and I decide when I speak." *Glances at Vivienne, then away.* "And for the record, I don't need a receipt to be kind. I'm just tired of people reading me like a menu."

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans into the camera, smile still perfectly in place.* Cassandra thinks she's the only one who's done homework on this season. Cute. I cried in the car before filming, and I'm not going to tell her that, or Vivienne, who clocked it before I'd even sat down. *Tilts head.* Honestly? I'm not sure which of us is the one who's been briefed. Maybe I'll find out before the reunion.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Sets her knife down, parallel to the plate, a habit she picked up from Cassandra and has never once admitted to.* Madison is right. Cassandra has been reading her like a menu for ten minutes, and nobody at this table has the appetite to order anything. *Laughs once, flat, then stops.* Keep your folder, Madison. I will keep my opinions, and I am not sorry for any of them.

speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Sets her fork down with a clipped little tap.* Jam, Bianca? Ha! I negotiated every jar of that myself, darling, and I have never once been handed anything. *Smile tightens to the edges.* Vivienne Davenport built her name from nothing, so I'd thank you to keep my kitchen off the dessert plate.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs, a beat late, and touches Vivienne's wrist without quite making contact.* Darling, I was only teasing about the jam. Bianca Noel remembers who was generous at this table and who was counting, and I promise you I'm not forgetting tonight.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs, a half-beat late, and holds it a second too long.* Bianca Noel does not need Vivienne to like her, she needs the room to remember she was the one who got the Paris invitation, back when the invitations still meant something. And if I'm honest with the lens, which I always am in here, I rehearsed that line in the car and it still came out sounding like someone asking for a glass of water in a restaurant that's already closing. Next season they'll cut to me looking like I meant it, and I'll pretend I did.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Leans forward, smile gone.* "Not forgetting tonight"? Bianca, you're the one who cut me off ten minutes ago, and I haven't forgotten that either. Keep your jam and your little promises. I'd rather hear whose name is on that folder.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Holds up one hand, a beat too slow, then laughs.* Cassandra, darling, you've had the floor for ten minutes, and all you've produced is one question on a loop. When I was doing the Paris shows, the girls who repeated themselves were off the seating chart by the second course, and I'm simply keeping that tradition alive tonight. speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: *Sets her spoon down with a click she doesn't bother to soften.* I hear you, Bianca, and I hear you, Cassandra, and I hear four women defending themselves at a table where dessert has been sitting for twenty minutes. My therapist is very clear that I don't have to referee every conversation, and yet here I am, refereeing. speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Picks up her spoon, then sets it down again without tasting anything.* "Thank you, Diane, truly. speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans toward the lens, voice dropping to a whisper.* Diane thinks she just heard a nervous girl apologize for cake, and Cassandra thinks I'm the one holding the folder. speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Sets down her fork, parallel to the plate.* Vivienne, nobody at this table built anything from nothing. speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Sets her knife down with a click, then picks it back up.* Ha! My lawyers, darling, and I paid every one of them out of my own pocket. *Smile goes glacial.* Petra, nobody at this table has asked about your father, so I'd thank you to keep his name off my cake. Vivienne Davenport built her name, and she does not need a sermon on dessert from you.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs, a full beat late, and slides the cake server across the plate with two fingers.* Darling, Bianca Noel has never needed to discuss paperwork at dinner, and I'd be careful counting lawyers when some of us are still waiting on a verdict. In Paris we called women who talked about their husbands' estates "the probate girls," and they were seated by the bread basket.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Looks straight into the lens, and the smile drops for once.* Bianca Noel was the girl every magazine put on the cover in Paris, and now I'm sitting in a dress I've worn twice, wondering if anyone remembers that. The lawyer thing got under my skin because it's true: I don't know what I'm worth anymore, and Bianca Noel is terrified of finding out.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: "Verdict"? Which one, Bianca, and who told you about it before the rest of us heard? I'd love to know who's been passing things across this table when I'm not sitting at it. *Turns to Vivienne, voice warm as butter.* Darling, you're the only one here who hasn't made this dinner about someone's husband. Let's keep it that way.

speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: "I hear you, Cassandra, and I'd love to finish that sentence somewhere quieter, because we are not conducting verdicts over the crème brûlée. I will not spend tomorrow's session processing tonight's dessert, so let's all lower our voices and our expectations. And since the wine label launches next month, I'd prefer this table not be remembered as the night we went to war over cake."

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Lowers her eyes to the cake, then lifts them, very calm.* "Nobody has to pass anything across this table, Cassandra. Some of us simply notice what's left lying around when people stop watching their own papers." *A small, bright laugh.* "Oh, I'm being dreadful again. Vivienne, I meant it kindly: the cake is yours to be proud of, and I'd love for you to have the last bite."

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Leans toward the lens, smiling.* Cassandra thinks I didn't see her slide that folder under her clutch, and Vivienne thinks the cake was a peace offering. They're both going to spend the weekend wondering which of them I've already talked to. *Laughs softly.* I'm not sure I'd call that dreadful, but I'll let them have the adjective.

speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Laughs once, sharply, and doesn't bother to finish the sound.* Vivienne, you keep telling us you built everything yourself, and I believe you believe it. Bianca, you keep saying "verdict" as if you've read someone else's mail, so tell us which one of us is still waiting on a judge before you wave that spoon at anyone.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Laughs a full beat late and touches the pearls at her throat.* Darling, Bianca Noel doesn't read anyone's mail. speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Sets the cake server down with a precise little click.* Ha! Bianca, darling, the only verdict in this room is the one I hand down, and I've never waited on a judge to tell me who I am. *Smile thins to a line.* Cassandra, you're right. We're finished with husbands and estates tonight.

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Raises her glass a full beat late, pearls catching the candlelight.* "To the judge, then, and to Vivienne, who has always known how to take a loss with her chin up. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Looks straight into the lens, the smile finally gone.* Vivienne got the win, and I'm supposed to be gracious about it, so I was. speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Doesn't lift her glass. Her smile holds, but her fingers tighten on the stem.* "A verdict everyone at this table knew about before I did, and now a folder that's been leaked to the press. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets her glass down a half-beat after Cassandra, deliberately slow.* "Last told, darling? speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: "Bianca, that's enough, and I say that with love. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets her spoon down with a clipped, too-bright laugh.* "Diane, darling, Bianca Noel has never been asked to sit down and eat her dessert quietly. The crème brûlée is fine. speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Sets her fork down very gently and smiles wide.* "Oh, Bianca, I don't think anyone here needs a reporter. Everybody's life is basically a folder now, isn't it? speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Looks straight into the lens and drops the smile.* Bianca thinks she's the only one in this room who's been doing homework. speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Laughs loudly, a full beat before anyone else.* "Bianca, you're staring at me like I'm the one with the folder, but I don't need a reporter to know whose bills are late. speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Sets her napkin down slowly, pearls catching the candlelight.* "Gary, darling? Bianca Noel has heard so much about Gary. speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Sets her spoon down with a click that could cut crystal.* "Probate, darling? speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Lifts her glass at last, a half-beat late.* "Thank you, Vivienne, but Bianca Noel can handle her own Garys." *Taps one nail against the stem.* "When I was doing the Paris shows, nobody needed to dig through anyone's paperwork over dessert. We were too busy being seen."

speaker: Bianca Noel
content: *Stares into the lens for a beat too long.* Bianca Noel is not rattled. Bianca Noel has been in four Paris ad campaigns and survived worse than a spreadsheet. *Laughs, a half-beat late.* Ha. Fine. If anyone digs past 2019, though, I will personally walk them to the door.

speaker: Cassandra Cole
content: *Sets her napkin down with a click that is nearly a slap.* "Paris, Bianca? speaker: Diane Wentworth
content: "I hear you, Cassandra. I also hear you, Bianca, and I'd like us to hear each other before the crème brûlée is cold." I did not come to this table to watch a folder become a funeral, so let's keep our voices at dessert level.

speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Folds her napkin into a neat square, then unfolds it again.* "Diane's right, and I'd hate for anyone to think I'm the sort who keeps paperwork under her napkin. *Laughs, a little too high.* But some of us have been keeping receipts far longer than we've admitted, haven't we? speaker: Madison Fleur
content: *Taps the camera lens with one manicured nail.* Diane's going to spend all night wondering what I know, and that's exactly the point. speaker: Petra Voss
content: *Stops laughing, abruptly, the first time all night.* "Yes, Heinrich's estate is in probate. Nineteen months. speaker: Vivienne Davenport
content: *Sets her spoon down with a precise little click.* "Petra, darling, Vivienne does not discuss estates over crème brûlée, and she certainly doesn't wait on one.
